notes: No accepted C++, so orig.cpp is a corpus-written reference after the official solution: (A)B is a binary-tree node with left A and right B, s1 reaches a right chain by operations 1-3 from the chain's foot, and s2 reaches one by inverse operation 4 from the root, so at most 3n operations (2.5n on --max). Operation sequences are not unique, so checker.py replays them on a treap (its C++ built like a reference) and compares the result with s2. The output passes on both samples, on 300 generated cases under a naive string replay, and the checker agrees with that replay on 400 mutated outputs.
